provenance.buyerQuestion: If a vendor makes a public claim, how do you know the proof behind it still holds?
provenance.targetQuery: how to check the proof behind a vendor's public claim still holds

source.quote: Root cause: six evidence bundles (SUBMAGIC-DEMO-LANE-PREFLIGHT, JSON2VIDEO-CAPTION-SEMANTICS-PREFLIGHT, PRODUCTION-ORCHESTRATION-PREFLIGHT, SUBMAGIC-LIVE-CONTRACT-FIX-V1, JSON2VIDEO-CAPTION-SEMANTICS-FIX-V1, and M1-REAL-PRODUCE-REVIEW-PUBLISH itself) pinned evidence to commit SHAs that do not exist anywhere in this repository's object store: not merged to main, not reachable from any ref, not even a surviving dangling object.

limitations: Commit message written by the product team for its own repair; it describes the defect, it does not independently prove it.

source.quote: a fresh disposable clone (the authoritative verification environment) never fetches an unreachable commit, so these bundles could never truly resolve there, baseline debt notwithstanding.

Critically, M1-REAL-PRODUCE-REVIEW-PUBLISH phantom pin was silently failing its own evidence bundle, which in turn silently forced derivePublicationCeiling back to candidate -- a live regression of the ratified SOS-PUBLICATION-DECISION-M1-V1 promotion, not a cosmetic data issue.

For the three preflight entries (research docs never merged to main, no product code, no public claim), evidence is repointed to CAPABILITIES.yaml own SOS-PUBLIC-TRUTH-V1 entry, which documents each preflight and its disclosed gap by name. For the three entries whose cited paths/tests are real, current-tree files, the phantom commit pin is dropped so resolution falls back to HEAD, per verify-evidence.ts own path-resolution rule.
Every claimCeiling/prohibitedClaims/publicationStatus value is unchanged; only the evidence citations used to verify those claims are repaired.
found ops:test RED on pristine canonical main (bd25233) as well, independent of the public-truth issue -- a second, separately-diagnosed baseline defect.
Both fixtures' own doc comments say they must break the day the real grant changes rather than silently keep passing -- they broke, correctly, and this is that break repaired
declaration.test.ts's integration smoke and the M1 public_marketable derivation both failed on pristine canonical main (bd25233), reproduced with zero FDTS product changes present.
Human-ratified promotion (T0/Marc): M1-REAL-PRODUCE-REVIEW-PUBLISH moves from publicationStatus candidate to public_marketable

slots.writingObjective: Name the repair in plain words, as a grounded fact about ShortsOS.
One sentence a search result can show: what was repaired, and that no public claim changed.
Open with the buyer's stake — a claim is only as good as the record behind it — then say that ShortsOS found such a gap in its own records.
slots.buyerIntent: Can I trust that a vendor's proof can still be checked?

slots.heading: What broke, and what was repaired?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: what the defect was, why a fresh copy could not check it, what the repair changed and what it left untouched.

slots.heading: Why a quiet failure mattered
slots.writingObjective: Explain that one broken record belonged to the capability ratified for the public claim, and that on a fresh copy it silently pushed that capability back to candidate status.
slots.buyerIntent: Did the defect affect what the vendor was allowed to claim?

slots.heading: How the repair was scoped
slots.writingObjective: Describe the two kinds of fix, that no claim wording or status changed, and the second, separate defect repaired the same day.
slots.buyerIntent: Was the fix narrow, or did it rewrite the claims?

slots.heading: What it means if you rely on the claim
slots.writingObjective: Bring it back to the buyer: proof has to be re-checkable by someone who was not there; say how ShortsOS reproduced the failure before fixing it and what each repaired record now points at.
slots.buyerIntent: What should I ask any vendor about its proof?
